reasons.plausibility: Al has low solubility in BCC refractory alloys and tends to form brittle intermetallics (e.g., B2, Laves phases) with Zr, Ti, and Hf, which would severely degrade ductility and likely strength, making the proposed solid-solution strengthening mechanism physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed test with graded Al substitutions and clear quantitative rejection criteria (density reduction <10%, strength drop >10%) is well-defined and would decisively falsify the hypothesis.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core trade-off but is based on a fundamentally flawed alloy design strategy, so testing it would waste resources and not advance the field.
